VI. The logical argument

  • is is not a strict mathematical proof. It is a transcendental-abductive argument.

Argument 1 — The concreteness argument

  • Conscious experience is a concrete occurrence.
  • Abstract computations are not concrete occurrences.
  • Therefore an abstract computation cannot itself be numerically identical with a conscious occurrence.
  • Any adequate theory must identify a concrete realization.
  • That realization must be individuated non-arbitrarily.
  • erefore:
  • oxed{
  • ext{consciousness requires a concrete bearer criterion}.

Argument 2 — The causal-efficacy argument

  • Human conscious states systematically influence reasoning, learning, memory, report, and action.
  • A theory that makes consciousness causally idle fails to explain this systematic alignment.
  • Abstract computational wholes can be causally redundant if every physical transition is fully explained at a lower implementation level.
  • A causally privileged macro-process can make a genuine difference through system-level constraint and control.
  • The candidate conscious bearer should therefore be a causally efficacious macro-process rather than an observer-imposed algorithmic description.
  • erefore:
  • oxed{
  • i^\ast
  • ext{ must possess real macro-causal organization}.
  • e CF Debate’s binding objection makes a related point: if the complex conscious whole adds no causal contribution beyond isolated computational steps, the resulting consciousness risks becoming epiphenomenal. ([The Co-Sentience Initiative][3])

Argument 3 — The binding argument

  • Experience contains multiple qualities co-present in one field.
  • Sequential local computations do not automatically constitute one intrinsic whole.
  • External observers can describe a collection as an algorithmic whole even if no causally active whole exists internally.
  • Therefore formal integration is insufficient.
  • The bearer must instantiate a concrete closure in which the constituents have reciprocal system-level consequences.
  • us:
  • oxed{
  • ext{co-presence requires constitutive closure,}
  • t mere:
  • ext{computational aggregation}.

Argument 4 — The valence argument

  • Consciousness is not ordinarily neutral information processing; states feel better, worse, urgent, boring, interesting, painful, relieving, or meaningful.
  • Externally assigned reward values cannot explain intrinsic mattering.
  • Self-maintaining biological systems possess objective stakes in their continued organization.
  • These stakes structure perception, memory, policy, and attention.
  • The same concrete process can therefore be described extrinsically as endogenous regulation and intrinsically as felt significance.

If qualia faded without the person noticing, the result appears incoherent; this is used to support functionalism. ([The Co-Sentience Initiative][4])

“Functionally identical” is ambiguous.
  • the replacement preserves only:

  • macro-causal influence;
  • intrinsic field-supporting physical organization.

XV. What the framework proves—and does not prove

It establishes by argument

  • A concrete conscious occurrence cannot be identical with an abstract computation.

  • Phenomenal causation is most parsimoniously preserved by token identity rather than interaction between separate substances.
  • Maximal closure across memory, value, counterfactuals, and reciprocal control is a stronger subject criterion than any single known boundary measure.

XVI. Final superior formulation

Appendix: Tantrāloka Integration

How the TĀ grounds each aperture component in textual evidence

1. Manifest discrimination (𝒥ᵢ) — jñāna/prakāśa

  • ĪPK 1.3.7:** "syād ekaś cid-vapur jñāna-smṛty-apohana-śaktimān" — consciousness has the power of cognition as one of three fundamental powers. [T]
  • TĀ 1.52:** "A thing without the nature of manifestation has neither manifestness nor reality." Manifestation is the condition under which any property can appear. [T]
  • TĀ 1.54:** "Manifestation shines everywhere at all times. Because it cannot be denied, what use are means of knowledge to establish it?" Even the attempt to deny manifestation occurs within manifestation. [T]
  • Key result:** Manifestation has transcendental priority. Not proven: manifestation is one cosmic subject.

2. Memory (ℳᵢ) — smṛti

  • ĪPK 1.3.7:** Memory is the second of the three fundamental powers. [T]
  • ĪPK 1.4.1-2 (Torella App.II):* Memory is NOT passive trace-retrieval but active reconstruction. The Yoga Sūtra definition ("anubhūtaviṣayāsampramoṣaḥ smṛtiḥ") is deliberately changed by Utpaladeva from *asampramoṣaḥ (static non-extinction) to asampramoṣaṇam (active non-extinction-ing), emphasizing memory as a function of the agent subject. [T]
  • The I as invariant:** Memory demonstrates that the "I" bridges past and present cognitions. The part-self (svātmāṃśe) is not limited by time, even though the part-object (arthāṃśe) belongs to the past. The one and same self-awareness (svasaṃvedana) of both cognitions creates the bridge that the Buddhist trace-model cannot explain. [T]
  • Key result:** Memory is active reconstruction linking past and present through an invariant first-person pole. Not proven: that this invariant is a timeless metaphysical self rather than a dynamically maintained trajectory.

3. Determination (ℰᵢ) — apohana

  • ĪPK 1.3.7:** Exclusion (apohana) is the third fundamental power — not an incidental linguistic operation but a constitutive power of consciousness. [T]
  • Torella App.I:** Utpaladeva transforms the Buddhist apoha (purely negative linguistic exclusion) into positive determination. The power of exclusion (apohana-śakti) operates when conceptual elaboration "delimits an object in space and time." For the Buddhists, "cow" = "not-non-cow" (purely negative). For Utpaladeva, exclusion is the positive act of determining "this as this." [T]
  • TĀ 3:17-18 (rāga-niyati):** "The principle of Attachment is just the craving itself for all objects; the principle of Restraint is that same craving when it arises with some particular fixed object." This pairs determination with desire: generalized reaching becomes specific fixation, producing a localized world. [T]
  • Key result:** Determination through exclusion is textually established as a power of consciousness. Not proven: that content exclusion (E_content) is the same operation as subject exclusion (E_subject — why one field is private).

4. Counterfactual generation (ℐᵢ) — vikalpa/imagination

  • ĪPK I.6.10:** "sa naisargika evāsti vikalpe svairacāriṇi / yathābhimatasaṃsthānābhāsanād buddhigocare" — imagination wanders autonomously (svairacārin), self-prompted (svapreraṇa), manifesting configurations at will (yathābhimata). This is the clearest ordinary evidence of svātantrya (freedom). [T]
  • ĪPK I.6.11:** "ata eva yathābhīṣṭasamullekhāvabhāsanāt / jñānakriye sphuṭe eva siddhe sarvasya jīvataḥ" — because imagination manifests objects at will, the powers of knowledge and action are evident in every living being, "from a worm to Brahmā." Imagination is a path to Recognition (pratyabhijñā). [T]
  • TĀ Vol 1 ~28356 (vīṇa passage):** "A person who is at one (tanmaya) with the music experiences the beauty (vaicitrya) in a large number of notes applied by a dexterous touch... even when duality appears, reality is nondual." The musician simultaneously generates, predicts, perceives, corrects, and evaluates the musical structure — an unusually tight loop of imagination → action → world → perception → self-modification. [T — from MVV, cited in TĀ commentary]
  • Key result:** Imagination provides the clearest ordinary evidence for finite creative freedom. Not proven: that this entails absolute metaphysical freedom (V₁ ⇏ V₅).

5. Endogenous valuation (𝒱ᵢ) — rāga/camatkāra

  • ĪPK 1.5.11 Vṛtti:** Vimarśa (reflexive awareness) IS rendered as camatkāra (aesthetic relish). The distinction between sentient and insentient IS the presence of camatkāra. [T]
  • ĪPK 2.4.20 Vivṛti:** Svātantrya (freedom) is developed in terms of camatkāra. Svātantryābhāvāt (absence of freedom) = camatkārābhāvāt (absence of aesthetic relish). [T]
  • PTv p. 19** (cited in TĀ Vol 1 commentary): "Supreme consciousness itself, the supreme Bhairava, which is perfectly full, because it is always by its very nature essentially the aesthetic relish of consciousness which is independent of all things and most free." [T]
  • TĀ Vol 5:4146:** The universe is "the condensation of the flood of the juice (rasa) of consciousness, that has assumed a fixed defined form." The cosmos IS condensed aesthetic relish. [T]
  • Rastogi extraction (Ch.5):** Two formulations of camatkāra: existential (ρᵢ — joyful valuation of everything as oneself) and experiential (νᵢ — aesthetic savoring). Existential camatkāra IS basal self-affection. Experiential camatkāra IS local valence. [R — Rastogi's reconstruction from Utpaladeva's texts]
  • Key result:** Consciousness IS self-affective, not neutral. Not proven: that regulatory weighting (Semᵢ, Vᵢ) entails felt valence (νᵢ). The adaptation-rate model is a candidate bridge.

6. Connective synthesis (𝒞ᵢ) — anusandhāna

  • TĀ 16.242:** "bhogyajñānaṃ nānyadeheṣv anusandhānam arhati" — "Knowledge that is enjoyed in one body cannot perform connective synthesis with other bodies." This is the strongest textual basis for local phenomenal exclusion. Anusandhāna connects cognitions within one body (Bᵢ) but not across bodies (Bⱼ). [T]
  • Formal result:** One field is the maximal domain over which connective synthesis can operate:
  • `
  • = {x | x can enter reciprocal anusandhāna within Bᵢ}
  • = MaximalConnectedDomain(Cᵢ)
  • `
  • Key result:** The body is the condition under which cognitions can be retained together, recognized together, compared, attributed to one stream, and integrated across time. Not proven: that maximal connective synthesis = phenomenal co-presence.

7. Developmental trajectory (Γᵢ) — spanda/kāla

  • TĀ 1.59cd-60ab:** "Space, time and form cannot divide up Śiva, Who is the Light of consciousness and independent of (all) else, because (space and the rest) are conditioned by thought constructs based on unity and diversity (bhedābheda)." Time is not an external container but a construction within consciousness. [T]
  • TĀ Vol 4 ~1110:** "The vital breath is the first manifestation of consciousness. The intellect and the rest depend upon it, because they are vitalized by it." Prāṇa is the bridge from consciousness to temporal embodiment — the pulse (spanda) that manifests as temporal structure. [T]
  • Kāla as a kañcuka:** Time is one of the five coverings — a freely assumed limitation that constrains access to non-present states. The weak scientific interpretation (time as finite temporal access) is supported; the strong interpretation (consciousness creates physical time) is not. [T]
  • Key result:** Temporal continuity is a constructed feature of the aperture, not a direct readout of physical time. Not proven: that the spanda model entails one universal subject rather than one processual dynamic.

8. Embodied realization (Bᵢ) — deha-kula

  • TĀ 10:12113-12125:** "saṁvit sarvātmikā dehabhedād yā saṅkucet tu ṣā / melake 'nyonyasaṅghaṭṭapratibimbād vikasvarā" — "Consciousness, which is all things, contracts due to the differences between the bodies... [and] returns to its state of ongoing expansion during a gathering, because of the mutual reflection taking place by their union with one another." [T]
  • TĀ 1 (Kula definition):** The body is "the aggregate of the vital breaths, organs of sense, gross elements etc." — the condensed condition of consciousness by virtue of its freedom. [T]
  • Reflection model (corrected):** The behavior of another subject within my stream is the reflection (pratibimba). The other stream is INFERRED as the original (bimba). Dⱼ ⊄ Dᵢ but Rⱼ→ᵢ ⊂ Dᵢ. The body is NOT the mirror; it is the DIFFERENTIATING CONDITION that makes reflection possible. Three models remain viable: (A) body as mirror, (B) consciousness as mirror with bodies as differentiating conditions, (C) relation as mirror. [T + correction from Ratié]
  • Key result:** Body differences contract consciousness; mutual reflection expands it. Not proven: that the body boundary IS the phenomenal boundary. Skin ≠ peripersonal space ≠ cognitive light cone ≠ phenomenal field.

9. Self-model (SMᵢ) — ahaṃkāra/vimarśa

  • TĀ 1.127:** "ahaṃrūpā tu saṃvittirnityā svaprathanātmikā" — "I-shaped consciousness is eternally self-manifesting." The "I" is not an ego added to consciousness but consciousness's own form. [T]
  • TĀ Vol 10 ~23762:** Ahaṅcamatkāra — "the aesthetic rapture of 'I am'." Selfhood IS wonder, not something that has wonder. [T]
  • Timalsina Aham paper (2020):** Three topographies of aham: (1) empirical ego — limited self identified with body; (2) subject of experience — the "I" that objectifies the ego; (3) absolute I-consciousness (pūrṇāhantā) — the "I" that embodies the totality. [R — from Timalsina's reconstruction of Abhinavagupta]
  • Key result:** The self-model is not a single thing but a spectrum from contracted (ego) to expanded (absolute I-consciousness). Not proven: that the absolute endpoint entails numerical identity across all subjects.
